Performers
The Tudor Consort (vocal ensemble), Michael Stewart (director) Documented

These are credits for the nominated recording, not the separate Hyperion performances consulted for programme notes. Individual singers and choir size are not identified.

[2] [3] [4]
Work version
Unaccompanied motet for cantus, altus, tenor, second tenor and bassus Documented

The five-part score is the motet, not the Mass of the same name. The album lists the motet as track 1 and the Mass movements separately. The choir’s exact performing edition and pitch are not identified.

[5] [6] [2]
Recorded
2007-07-29 Inferred, not documented

FMA describes a live minidisc recording and gives the album date as 29 July 2007. The choir’s own archive documents the matching Renaissance Influences programme on that date. Their conjunction supports a probable session date, but the track description does not explicitly identify the session day. The FMA track’s 20 August 2010 is its online release.

[3] [4]
Place
Sacred Heart Cathedral, Hill Street, Wellington, New Zealand Inferred, not documented

The official archive supplies the venue for the matching 29 July 2007 concert. The link between that concert and the recording is inferred from title, director, programme and album date, not stated in the track description.

[4] [3]
Label
Unknown Unknown

No original recording label or commercial imprint is named; Free Music Archive is the distribution platform.

[3]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

The album title and track number are known, but no release catalogue number is supplied.

[3]
Transfer
Commons import from FMA by ComputerHotline Documented

The recording or minidisc-transfer engineer is not named. The uploader credit does not imply that ComputerHotline made the original recording.

[1] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The online track release is 20 August 2010; the Commons upload is 11 April 2020. No separate minidisc transfer or mastering date is established.

[1] [2] [3]
Processing
Live minidisc source; FMA MP3 converted to Ogg for Commons, with Wikimedia MP3 access derivative Documented

The source format chain is described by the album and Commons source entry. Microphone placement, equalisation, noise reduction and any earlier editing are unknown. No additional trim by Contrapunctus.

[3] [1]
Composition rights
Public-domain sixteenth-century motet Inferred, not documented

The 1569 work and public-domain 1862 score are distinct from the Tudor Consort’s modern performance rights.

[5] [7] [6]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — CC BY 3.0 Unported Documented

The external FMA track was opened directly and explicitly licenses the Tudor Consort performance under CC BY 3.0; no NonCommercial restriction is attached. Commons still displays a pending external licence review, so that template is not treated as a passed review. Independent FMA evidence supports the actual sound recording licence.

[2] [3] [1] [9]

Palestrina, Sicut lilium inter spinas; The Tudor Consort, directed by Michael Stewart. Live minidisc recording from Renaissance Influences; probably 29 July 2007, Sacred Heart Cathedral, Wellington. Source: The Tudor Consort / Free Music Archive; Commons import by ComputerHotline. Recording CC BY 3.0; transcoded access copy, no new editorial audio cut. Rights statement
